extracted.intended_audience: Project owners, Public Housing Agencies (PHAs), processing entities, HUD staff, and applicants/participants in HUD-assisted housing programs
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts regulatory requirements in 24 CFR Part 5 covering SSN/EIN disclosure and verification, consent and income-information procedures (including mandated use of EIV), penalties and appeal/verification procedures, plus pet-ownership rules for projects for the elderly or persons with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of assistance applicants (SSN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each assistance applicant must submit the complete and accurate SSN assigned to the assistance applicant and to each member of the assistance applicant's household when the assistance applicant's eligibility under the program involved is being determined (§ 5.216(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also required: documentation to verify each SSN as described in paragraph (g)(1). Section inapplicable to individuals who do not contend eligible immigration status under subpart E (see § 5.508).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of individual owner applicants (SSN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual owner applicant must submit the complete and accurate SSN assigned to the individual owner applicant and to each member of the individual owner applicant's household who will be obligated to pay the debt evidenced by the mortgage or loan documents when eligibility is being determined (§ 5.216(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also required: documentation to verify each SSN as described in paragraph (g)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of certain officials of entity applicants (SSN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each officer, director, principal stockholder, or other official of an entity applicant must submit the complete and accurate SSN assigned to each such individual and the documentation referred to in paragraph (g)(1) to verify each SSN (§ 5.216(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when entity applicant's eligibility under the program involved is being determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of participants — initial disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participant (except certain elderly grandfathered cases) must submit the SSN and verification documentation if the participant has not previously disclosed an SSN, previously disclosed an SSN that HUD or SSA determined was invalid, or been issued a new SSN; submission occurs at the next interim or regularly scheduled reexamination or recertification or other reexamination for the program involved (§ 5.216(e)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: participants age 62 or older whose initial determination of eligibility began before Jan 31, 2010 are excluded from this initial disclosure requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of participants — subsequent disclosure when adding household members
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a participant has disclosed and the processing entity has verified SSNs, when adding a new household member who is at least 6 years of age, or under 6 and already assigned an SSN, the participant must provide the SSN and verification documentation at the time of request or processing of the interim reexamination or recertification (§ 5.216(e)(2)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new members under age 6 with no assigned SSN, the participant must provide the SSN and verification documentation within 90 calendar days of adding the child; processing entity may grant one additional 90-day extension at its discretion for unforeseeable circumstances (§ 5.216(e)(2)(ii)). During the waiting period the child is included as part of the assisted household and entitled to benefits; failure to produce SSN after the time period triggers follow-up under § 5.218.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of participants — assignment of new SSN
rubrics_metrics.description: If a participant or household member is assigned a new SSN, the participant must submit the complete and accurate new SSN and verification documentation either at time of receipt, at the next interim or regularly scheduled reexamination or recertification, or at an earlier time specified by the processing entity (§ 5.216(e)(2)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing entity may set an earlier time for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of entity applicants (EIN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entity applicant must submit any complete and accurate EIN assigned to the entity applicant and the documentation referred to in paragraph (g)(2) to verify the EIN when the entity applicant's eligibility under the program involved is being determined (§ 5.216(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation requirements described in paragraph (g)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documentation to verify SSN
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentation necessary to verify an individual's SSN is: (i) a valid SSN card issued by the SSA; (ii) an original document issued by a federal or state government agency containing the individual's name and SSN with other identifying information; or (iii) such other evidence of the SSN as HUD may prescribe in administrative instructions (§ 5.216(g)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing entities must accept the listed documents; HUD may prescribe additional evidence in administrative instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documentation to verify EIN
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentation necessary to verify an entity applicant's EIN is the official, written communication from the Internal Revenue Service assigning the EIN, or such other evidence of the EIN as HUD may prescribe in administrative instructions (§ 5.216(g)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing entities should accept IRS assignment letter or HUD-prescribed alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on assistance applicants of failure to provide SSN documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for limited exceptions, if processing entity determines an assistance applicant is otherwise eligible, the assistance applicant may retain its place on the waiting list but cannot become a participant until it provides SSN documentation to verify each household member's SSN (§ 5.216(h)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules allow time-limited admission for certain SRO applicants and recent additions of children under 6 (90 days plus discretionary 90-day extension). Failure to produce documentation within required time leads to following § 5.218 provisions (§ 5.216(h)(2)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of SSN/EIN documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The processing entity must not reject documentation referred to in paragraph (g) of this section, except as HUD may otherwise prescribe through publicly issued notice (§ 5.216(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing entities are limited in their discretion to reject documents and must follow HUD notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for failing to disclose and verify SSNs/EINs — denial of eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing entity must deny eligibility of an assistance applicant or individual owner applicant if they do not meet the applicable SSN disclosure, documentation, and verification requirements specified in § 5.216 (§ 5.218(a)). For entity applicants, denial if EIN requirements or officials' SSN requirements are not met (§ 5.218(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial must be in accordance with provisions governing the specific program involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for failing to disclose and verify SSNs/EINs — termination of participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing entity must terminate the assistance or tenancy (or both) of a participant and the participant's household if the participant does not meet the applicable SSN disclosure, documentation, and verification requirements specified in § 5.216 (§ 5.218(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing entity may defer termination and grant an additional 90 calendar days only if failure was due to unforeseen circumstances outside participant control and there is reasonable likelihood of compliance (§ 5.218(c)(2)); failure to disclose by deadline results in termination (§ 5.218(c)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent requirement for income-information access
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member of the family who is at least 18 years of age, and each family head and spouse regardless of age, shall sign one or more consent forms authorizing HUD/PHAs to obtain income information (§ 5.230(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent is required from applicants and participants per timing rules; computer matches require certification that consent and Privacy Act notice have been provided (§ 5.234).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and renewal of consent forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit signed consent forms when eligibility is being determined. Prior to January 1, 2024 participants signed at each regularly scheduled income reexamination; on or after January 1, 2024, participants must sign at their next interim or regularly scheduled reexamination and after all adult family members have signed once on or after that date they need not sign again except when a new adult joins, a member turns 18, or as required by HUD/PHA administrative instructions (§ 5.230(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs and participants must follow the post-2024 single-signature rule with specified exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of consent form
rubrics_metrics.description: Consent forms must at minimum: (1) authorize HUD and PHAs to obtain SWICA information; (2) authorize HUD, PHAs, or owners to verify income information with employers; (3) authorize HUD to request income return information from the IRS and SSA solely to verify income; (4) authorize PHAs to obtain financial records from financial institutions when needed; and (5) state that authorization remains effective until final adverse decision, cessation of eligibility, or express revocation (§ 5.230(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent must include Privacy Act and Right to Financial Privacy Act considerations; authorization duration and revocation conditions must be stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for failing to sign consent forms
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant/participant or any family member required to sign does not sign and submit the consent form, then the processing entity shall deny assistance to and admission of an assistance applicant; assistance and tenancy of a participant may be terminated (§ 5.232(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section does not apply if a family member revokes consent for PHAs to access financial institution records unless the PHA establishes a policy that revocation will result in denial or termination (§ 5.232(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandated use of HUD's Enterprise Income Verification (EIV) system
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing entities administering assistance under listed programs (public housing, HCV, moderate rehabilitation, project-based programs, certain Section 202/811 and other identified programs) must use HUD's EIV system in its entirety as a third-party source to verify employment and income information during annual and streamlined reexaminations and to reduce administrative and subsidy payment errors (§ 5.233(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use must be in accordance with § 5.236 and HUD administrative guidance. Failure to use EIV in its entirety may result in sanctions and/or assessment of disallowed costs associated with incorrect subsidy or tenant rent calculations (§ 5.233(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and certification for requests from SWICAs and Federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Income information will generally be obtained through computer matching agreements; certification that appropriate consent forms and Privacy Act notice were provided is required (the processing entity certifies to HUD or to the SWICA as applicable) (§ 5.234(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions on use of SWICA/IRS/SSA income information apply per 42 U.S.C. 3544(c)(2)(A) and 26 U.S.C. 6103(l)(7). Computer matching agreements must specify purpose, legal authority, records to be matched, disposition of matched info, safeguards, use/restrictions on duplication/redisclosure, certification, and processing charges (§ 5.234(b)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for independent verification and when to pursue verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any determination/redetermination of family income verified under § 5.236(b) must follow requirements applicable to the individual covered program. Upon receiving SWICA/Federal agency income info, HUD/PHAs shall compare it to the family's provided information and may pursue independent verification (including requesting information from undisclosed employers) when undisclosed income sources are revealed or when information differs substantially (§ 5.236(b)(1)-(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD/PHAs may verify directly with applicants/participants; verification need not be pursued when sums are too small to infer fraud or justify verification expense; HUD/PHAs may inform owners to verify, and owners must not be given SWICA income information (unless the PHA is the owner); SSA/IRS disclosure restrictions apply (§ 5.236(b)(4)-(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to contest adverse findings from matches
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD, the PHA, or the owner shall promptly notify any assistance applicant or participant in writing of adverse findings made on the basis of verified information; the assistance applicant or participant may contest the findings in the same manner as other eligibility information, and termination/denial/suspension shall not occur until any notice period required by statute or program regulations has expired (§ 5.236(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and contest procedures must follow the program-specific requirements governing eligibility disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal and civil penalties for improper use/disclosure of income information
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who violate 42 U.S.C. 3544 or 26 U.S.C. 6103(l)(7) with respect to use and disclosure of income information may be subject to civil or criminal penalties under 42 U.S.C. 3544(c)(3), 26 U.S.C. 7213(a), or 18 U.S.C. 1905 (§ 5.238).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This warns processing entities and individuals of potential statutory sanctions for misuse or improper disclosure of sensitive income information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family disclosure of HUD notices and verification duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Families in assisted units must promptly furnish to the responsible entity any HUD letter or notice to a family member concerning amount or verification of family income (§ 5.240(b)). The responsible entity must verify the accuracy of income information received from the family and change payments or terminate assistance as appropriate (§ 5.240(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely family cooperation is required to enable accurate tenant rent and subsidy calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and purpose of pet-ownership subpart for elderly/disabled projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart C implements statutory protections relating to pet ownership for projects for the elderly or persons with disabilities under specified HUD programs; it applies to housing programs administered by the Assistant Secretary for Housing-Federal Housing Commissioner, certain chapter VIII programs, and the public housing program (§ 5.300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the regulatory scope for following pet-owner protections and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for animals that assist persons with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart C does not apply to animals used to assist, support, or provide service to persons with disabilities; project owners and PHAs may not apply or enforce policies under this subpart against such animals; exclusion applies to animals residing in or visiting projects for the elderly or persons with disabilities (§ 5.303(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart C does not limit rights of persons with disabilities nor affect other authority to regulate assistance animals under federal, state, or local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of common household pet
rubrics_metrics.description: For Housing programs: a domesticated animal traditionally kept in the home for pleasure (dog, cat, bird, rodent including rabbit, fish, or turtle). Common household pet does not include reptiles (except turtles) and does not include animals used to assist persons with disabilities. If conflict with State/local law defining pets exists, State/local law applies (§ 5.306).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs may define the term differently for Public Housing programs under § 5.318; owners using Housing programs must use the Part 5 definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against discrimination based on pet ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise specifically authorized, no project owner or PHA that owns or manages a project for the elderly or persons with disabilities may, as a condition of tenancy or otherwise, prohibit or prevent any tenant from owning common household pets or discriminate against any person in admission or continued occupancy because of pet ownership (§ 5.309).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a baseline protection preventing blanket pet bans in covered projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to tenants regarding pet rules
rubrics_metrics.description: During development of pet rules, the project owner or PHA must serve written notice on all tenants stating that tenants are permitted to own and keep common household pets in accordance with pet rules; service animals are excluded; tenants may request copies of current or proposed pet rules; tenants may request lease amendments to permit common household pets (§ 5.312(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/PHAs must also give applicants the notice when offered a unit and PHAs that choose not to promulgate pet rules must serve notice within 60 days of the part's effective date (§ 5.312(b)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of pet rules — mandatory and discretionary provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Project owners shall prescribe reasonable rules to govern keeping of common household pets and must include mandatory rules described in § 5.350; they may also include discretionary provisions as provided in § 5.318. PHAs may choose not to promulgate rules; if they do, tenants must be permitted to own and keep pets consistent with leases, this subpart, and state/local law (§ 5.315(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pet rules must be reasonably related to furthering legitimate interests (e.g., decent, safe, sanitary environment; protecting property) and drawn narrowly to achieve those interests without unnecessary burdens. Owners/PHAs may vary rules among projects based on size, type, location, occupancy, provided rules remain reasonable and not conflict with state/local law (§ 5.315(c)-(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary pet-rule factors — definitions and density
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules promulgated by owners/PHAs may include, but are not limited to: definitions of 'common household pet' (PHAs may define for Public Housing; housing program owners must use § 5.306 definition) and consideration of tenant and pet density, including reasonable limitations on the number of common household pets allowed per dwelling unit (§ 5.318(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/PHAs may consider unit/project-specific factors when setting limits (size, occupancy, etc.), but limits must be reasonable and consistent with other subpart requirements.
